task: Fix the incorrect access control after the role inheritance chain was updated.

candidate_memories.content: Reviewer role now has write access to configuration settings after the role inheritance chain was changed.
Reviewer role must inherit from ReadOnly, not from Editor; the inheritance was changed by mistake in the last deploy.
The role inheritance config is in access/roles.yaml; the Reviewer entry must reference ReadOnly as its parent.
After any role inheritance change, run a full permission regression test before deploying to production.
The misconfiguration only affects the Reviewer role; the Contributor and Owner roles are unaffected.
The RBAC system was migrated from a flat role model to an inheritance-based model in 2023.
Session 4 note: the admin panel was updated to show role inheritance chains visually.
Old lesson: flat RBAC models were simpler to audit but harder to manage as the role count grew.
The permission cache is refreshed every 5 minutes; a fresh session will pick up role changes immediately.
Session 10 note: the security team completed a quarterly access review and found no violations.
Old RBAC guide: Reviewer role had direct write access to configuration before the inheritance model was introduced.
Role inheritance chains must be documented and tested for unintended permission escalation.
The compliance team requested a role audit report in session 14.
Roles are also used to filter analytics dashboards; the Reviewer role sees aggregate-only metrics.
Session 7 note: a new Analyst role was added for the data team without write access.
The role inheritance config is deployed via GitOps and requires a two-person approval.
When modifying role inheritance, test both the changed role and all roles that inherit from it.
Session 11 note: the support team role was restricted to read-only access.
Old RBAC config: Reviewer and Editor shared the same parent role before the inheritance refactor.
The API enforces role checks at both the gateway level and the service handler level.
